channel: interop-🌃/_threads/Besu only builds on empty blocks
searchText: I look into that Looks like that is an issue with the shadow fork. The shadow fork is around 2,500 blocks behind real Sepolia. Before the Glamsterdam hardfork Besu connects to regular Sepolia nodes, which are not part of the shadow fork, and those report that their head is those 2,500 blocks ahead. Because of that Besu thinks it needs to sync and during sync disables the tx pool. That explains the empty blocks. Once we fork off to Glamsterdam on the shadow fork we disconnect the regular Sepolia peers and only get the ones from the shadow fork. At this point the head of our peers and Besu is the same and we enable the tx pool again. We need to check how to do that differently, even though that is only shadow fork specific and does not happen on real networks This merged PR should fix that issue: https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/11424 nice <@577788234810130432> Seems the Besu version on sepsf-2 is 26.9.0 and not the latest from commit from main. So the Besu nodes again are proposing empty blocks. ethpandaops/besu:main should contain the fix we run releases on shadowforks can you make a release before the gloas fork? No, a release takes several days of testing to make sure nothing breaks. We have one planned for early next week, but for this shadow fork it’s too late

excerpts.content: Looks like that is an issue with the shadow fork. The shadow fork is around 2,500 blocks behind real Sepolia. Before the Glamsterdam hardfork Besu connects to regular Sepolia nodes, which are not part of the shadow fork, and those report that their head is those 2,500 blocks ahead. Because of that Besu thinks it needs to sync and during sync disables the tx pool. That explains the empty blocks. Once we fork off to Glamsterdam on the shadow fork we disconnect the regular Sepolia peers and only get the ones from the shadow fork. At this point the head of our peers and Besu is the same and we enable the tx pool again.
